title: What is stonewalling?
question: Why does leaving without a word make the other person feel rejected?

paragraphs.text: Psychologist John Gottman and his colleagues watched couples talk for 15 minutes.
They predicted which couples would divorce with 93% accuracy.
They named four behaviours that signal a break-up.
The four horsemen are criticism, defensiveness, contempt and stonewalling.
These behaviours also harm working relationships, including between a leader and their team.
Blame, contempt and stonewalling damage trust and disrupt work.
Stonewalling means withdrawing from a conversation.
You go quiet, change the subject or leave the room.
paragraphs.note: This lists your actions. The question asks why the other person feels rejected.

paragraphs.text: It usually happens when you feel overwhelmed.
paragraphs.note: This explains your feelings. The question asks about the other person.

paragraphs.text: The other person can't see that.
They see you withdraw without a word and feel ignored or rejected.
